text:
emma: quick spike question — do we want to introduce a concept of a key 'steward' (team/service) separate from the creating project? we're running into churn when projects are archived and keys become orphaned.
diego: +1 for explicit steward. projects are too volatile. steward maps better to operational responsibility.
priya: if we add steward, need to decide the policy surface: who can view secret, who can rotate, who can transfer. my vote: steward+security-admins can do all; delegated runners (service-accounts) can rotate only.
sam: operationally, transfer should be a guarded flow. require current steward confirmation OR an approval ticket. no silent transfers.
emma: also think about labeling keys with "sensitivity" (device, infra, billing) so rotation cadence and vaulting rules vary. sensitivity=HIGH keys must be HSM-backed and require co-approval to transfer.
diego: implementation note: add fields `steward_type`, `steward_id`, `sensitivity`, and `steward_state`(INFERRED|ASSIGNED|LOCKED). migration will mark existing null steward as INFERRED with a TTL.
priya: how do we infer steward? heuristics: last committer in repo, last servicing team in deployment manifest, or last person to rotate. mark with provenance and ping the inferred steward list.
sam: I want an automated sweep that compiles all keys referenced in k8s secrets, terraform state, and repo config. show an inventory with "referenced-by" rows in the UI to help steward claim.
audit-bot: Note: add webhook event audit.key.steward_assigned with payload {key_id, old_steward, new_steward, changed_by, reason, incident_id?}.
diego: rotation model: allow scheduled rotations for delegated runners, manual rotate for stewards, and emergency rotate for security-admins. emergency rotate should generate a short-lived rollback token (valid 20m) to restore old key if we break things.
emma: UI/UX: transfer modal should be two-step: confirm recipient + sanity checklist that lists impacted services plus a rotation option. if recipient declines within 48h, transfer fails.
priya: RBAC matrix idea: actions = [view_metadata, view_secret, rotate, transfer, revoke]. default grants: steward -> all; delegated_runner -> rotate, view_metadata; security_admin -> all and emergency_rotate.
sam: for cross-org infra keys (shared billing webhooks, partner integrations) introduce steward_type=GLOBAL and require 2-person auth for transfer/revoke. also allow a read-only "usage" group to inspect referenced-by footprint.
diego: migration plan sketch: 1) run inventory + inference job, 2) open notice to inferred stewards, 3) auto-assign placeholder steward after 14d and create follow-up tickets, 4) enable steward-based RBAC in soft mode, 5) enforce after 30d.
emma: DB migration example: "UPDATE api_keys SET steward_state='INFERRED' WHERE steward_id IS NULL;" include a backfill job that writes provenance into audit log.
priya: tests: policy unit tests for RBAC combinations, e2e for transfer modal (accept/decline), migration dry-run against snapshot. add canary rotation test that rotates in staging and verifies auth acceptance rates.
sam: ops runbook: when rotating keys used by many envs, perform staged rollout: rotate in test -> staging -> 30% prod -> 100% prod, with a health check and ability to rollback using rollback token.
audit-bot: RFC follow-up: SEC-KEYS-STEWARD-2026 created. webhook posted to #audit-stream.
emma: question for API design: should transfers be POST /keys/:id/transfer with {to_steward, require_rotation}? or should we have a two-step accept endpoint?
diego: two-step better: POST creates transfer_request record, steward must call POST /transfer/:id/accept. transfer_request should include a TTL and optionally auto-rotate.
priya: agree. also allow programmatic transfer with signed approval artifact for automation workflows. store artifact hash in audit trail.
sam: minor: show "last-seen" auth fingerprint in UI (last auth timestamp + service fingerprint) so stewards know if key is actively used. helps decide whether to rotate during transfer.
emma: i'll draft the follow-up note with DB patch, API contract, UI mock, and a migration timeline. will ping reviewers @priya @diego. thanks all. :thumbsup:
